title: Loan Agreement Schedule — Borrowing Base Reporting Covenants of the Operating Lines of Credit
content:
Some Operating Lines of Credit lend against a borrowing base reported by the member on signed borrowing base certificates. This schedule states, for every product, whether a borrowing base applies and the reporting periods that go with it.

## Covenant terms

- **Borrowing base required**: whether advances are limited by the borrowing base of the latest certificate.
- **Certificate frequency**: the calendar days between required borrowing base certificates; 0 means no certificate is required.
- **Certificate staleness**: the calendar days after a certificate's as-of date through which it may still support an advance; 0 means not applicable.
- **Deficiency cure period**: the calendar days after a certificate shows outstanding principal above the borrowing base within which the shortfall must be repaid; 0 means not applicable.
- **Oldest receivable**: the oldest a receivable may be, in calendar days from invoice, to count toward the borrowing base; 0 means not applicable.

## Schedule

| Product | Borrowing base required | Certificate frequency (calendar days) | Certificate staleness (calendar days after as-of date) | Deficiency cure period (calendar days) | Oldest receivable counted (calendar days from invoice) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| StartRight Operating Line | No | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| ExpressLine Operating Credit | No | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Seasonal Operating Loan | No | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Revolving Operating Line | No | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Borrowing Base Operating Line | Yes | 30 | 45 | 10 | 90 |
| Agribusiness Revolving Line | Yes | 30 | 40 | 5 | 90 |

## Points of reading

- Only the Borrowing Base Operating Line and the Agribusiness Revolving Line are lent against a borrowing base; on the other four products every period in this schedule is 0, meaning not applicable.
- Both borrowing base products call for a certificate every 30 calendar days, but a certificate stays usable for advances somewhat longer: 45 calendar days after its as-of date on the Borrowing Base Operating Line and 40 on the Agribusiness Revolving Line.
- *Hypothetical illustration:* an invoice dated 1 March is 90 calendar days old on 30 May, the last day it still counts on either borrowing base product.
